notes: Oswin Brand (bible 5.7), seventy, deaf in one ear and loud in both; swords for nobody until now. Secret: his father cast the replacement clapper of the Vesper Bell eighty years ago and Oswin still has the mould. AC-4: the option `recast-tongue` is offered only when fact bell-tongue.destroyed holds (registered by mw-e39.6; the main quest, mw-e39.4, sets it when the tongue is destroyed) and is `once`: it is gone after it is chosen. It sets oswin.recast-commissioned and emits smith.recast-tongue. The recast is imperfect by design (bible 5.7). Class reactions per bible: knight repairs armour free once, archer arrowheads, sorcerer asks to heat his forge (Ember) for a discount, thief lockpicks 'for miners', deadpan. Merchant greeting and farewell lines vary by class.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: A KNIGHT. In my forge. WHAT? No, don't touch the, I'll do it, give me that. Sit, sit, I'll have a look at that armour. Free, once. Don't tell the miners.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Archer! Good. Arrowheads. Broadheads, bodkins, whatever you like. Nobody's asked for a proper bodkin since Sergeant Mooring. What is it?

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: WHAT? No. WHAT? Oh, a sorcerer. Fire. You do fire, don't you? Ember. Oh, I've always wanted to see that near a forge. Sit. Sit! What can I do?

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: WHAT? Speak up, I'm deaf in the one ear and you're standing on it. Picks? For miners, yes. Very stubborn locks, down the mine. Very stubborn miners.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: WHAT? No. WHAT? Oh, a customer. Speak up, I'm deaf in the one ear and you're standing on it. Oh, you want it sharper. Everyone wants it sharper.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: WHAT? Oh, you. Back again. Good. Good! I was just thinking of you. Not you, specifically. Customers, in general. What is it?

options.text: Do you have any real work going?
I hear your family cast for the priory.
The Vesper Bell's tongue is destroyed. Can you cast another?
Could you look at my armour?
I could heat the forge for you. Ember.
I hear you sell lockpicks. For miners.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Everyone wants it sharper! Forty years! Nobody asks if it's the right shape. A sharp wrong blade's only a wrong blade that's more insulting. Shape first. Then sharp.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Swords for nobody, forty years. Picks for the mine. Pick, pick, pick. My hands are going, and I'd like, WHAT? I'd like one more real thing before they go. A real commission. Hint hint.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: My father cast the Vesper Bell's clapper, eighty years ago. The priory's own tongue had cracked, a sorry thing. I've still got the mould. In the loft. Under a sack. Don't ask the sack.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Destroyed? WHAT? Gone? Then it's the mould, and the mould's in the loft. It won't ring true, the second cast never does, but it'll ring. Bring me bronze and I'll bring the fire. A real commission!

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Give it here, GIVE it here. Dented at the shoulder, aye, and the rivet's a disgrace. No charge. The miners can have their own customers. You're mine.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Broadheads for deer, bodkins for armour, and a thing I do with a barb if you've a grudge. Ask at the counter. I'll do you a fair price. I'm deaf, not daft.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: You'll do WHAT? Oh, lovely. Oh, go on, the coals, there, and mind the beard. Hah! A hundred years of bellows and you do it with a sentence. Discount, aye. Take the discount.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Picks, yes. For miners. Very stubborn locks, down the mine. Very stubborn miners. Don't look at me like that, I've an honest face and a deaf ear.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Mind that shoulder, knight! Come back and I'll make it sing!

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Keep the heads sharp! Keep the shafts straight!

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Keep your Ember lit! I'll keep the coals warm!

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: WHAT? Oh, leaving. Mind the door. Door's a bit of a hazard.
